assertions:
# Authorising an AI agent's tool calls: mirrors examples/agent_authz.py (keep the two in
# step). An agent never holds more authority than the person it acts for.
#   Gate 1 (tools/list): tool#invoke@agent, a lookup.
#   Gate 2 (a call): all three of agent#acts_for@person, tool#invoke@agent and
#   resource#view@person. A fixture checks each separately; the call is allowed only
#   when all three hold.
# Uses the pemba `steps:` extension (docs/07-testing.md §3.2) for the revocation.

# The example's four calls, all by agent:triage:
#   read roadmap for anne   allowed: all three gates hold
#   read payroll for anne   denied: anne cannot view payroll
#   read payroll for bea    denied: triage does not act for bea (bea can view payroll)
#   send_email for anne     denied: send_email was never granted
assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - agent:triage#acts_for@user:anne
    - tool:read_document#invoke@agent:triage
    - tool:search_documents#invoke@agent:triage
    - document:roadmap#view@user:anne
    - document:payroll#view@user:bea
  assertFalse:
    - document:payroll#view@user:anne
    - agent:triage#acts_for@user:bea
    - tool:send_email#invoke@agent:triage

expectedLookups:
  resources:
    # Gate 1: the agent's tools/list.
    - query: "tool#invoke@agent:triage"
      expect: [read_document, search_documents]
    - query: "document#view@user:anne"
      expect: [roadmap]
  subjects:
    - query: "agent:triage#acts_for@user"
      expect: { ids: [anne] }

steps:
  # Revocation: with the delegation gone, gate 2 denies every call, though the tool
  # grants and anne's own access are unchanged.
  - ops:
      - delete: agent:triage#principal@user:anne
    assertions:
      assertTrue:
        - tool:read_document#invoke@agent:triage
        - document:roadmap#view@user:anne
      assertFalse:
        - agent:triage#acts_for@user:anne
relationships:

document:roadmap#viewer@user:bea

# k + 1 and f00#viewer at depth k + 2. So f48 (f00#viewer at 50) answers; f49 (51) does not.
# Uses the pemba `expectCheckErrors:` extension (docs/07-testing.md §3.2).

    - folder:f48#view@user:root

  assertFalse:
    # f30 → f00 is 31 folders; nobody is anywhere on it.
    - folder:f30#view@user:near

expectCheckErrors:

  document:deep#view@user:root: MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED
  # A `false` needs the whole chain walked too.
  folder:f59#view@user:nobody: MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED

assertions:
# Direct relations, and Create / Touch / Delete visibility across write batches.
# Uses the pemba `steps:` extension (docs/07-testing.md §3.2); `zed validate` sees only
# the top-level relationships and assertions (step 0).

assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - document:readme#viewer@user:anne
    - document:readme#view@user:anne
    - document:readme#view@user:bob
    - document:readme#editor@user:bob
    - document:spec#view@user:carol
  assertFalse:
    - document:readme#editor@user:anne
    - document:readme#viewer@user:bob
    - document:readme#view@user:carol
    - document:spec#view@user:anne
    - document:readme#view@user:dan
    - document:unknown#view@user:anne

steps:
  # Create of a new tuple is visible.
  - ops:
      - create: document:readme#viewer@user:dan
    assertions:
      assertTrue:
        - document:readme#view@user:dan

  # Create of a live tuple fails the whole batch: erin's tuple is not written either.
  - ops:
      - create: document:spec#viewer@user:erin
      - create: document:readme#viewer@user:anne
    expectError: ALREADY_EXISTS
    assertions:
      assertTrue:
        - document:readme#view@user:anne
      assertFalse:
        - document:spec#view@user:erin

  # Touch of a live tuple is a no-op; touch of a new one creates it.
  - ops:
      - touch: document:readme#viewer@user:anne
      - touch: document:spec#editor@user:erin
    assertions:
      assertTrue:
        - document:readme#view@user:anne
        - document:spec#view@user:erin
        - document:spec#editor@user:erin

  # Delete removes; delete of an absent tuple is a no-op. Other tuples are untouched.
  - ops:
      - delete: document:readme#viewer@user:anne
      - delete: document:readme#viewer@user:nobody
    assertions:
      assertTrue:
        - document:readme#view@user:bob
        - document:readme#view@user:dan
      assertFalse:
        - document:readme#view@user:anne
        - document:readme#viewer@user:anne

  # A deleted tuple can be created again.
  - ops:
      - create: document:readme#viewer@user:anne
    assertions:
      assertTrue:
        - document:readme#view@user:anne

  # The same tuple twice in one batch is refused; nothing is applied.
  - ops:
      - touch: document:spec#viewer@user:frank
      - delete: document:spec#viewer@user:frank
    expectError: DUPLICATE_IN_BATCH
    assertions:
      assertFalse:
        - document:spec#view@user:frank

  # Deleting the only grant revokes the permission.
  - ops:
      - delete: document:readme#editor@user:bob
    assertions:
      assertFalse:
        - document:readme#view@user:bob

schema:
definition user {}

definition organization {
    relation owner: user
    relation member: user
    permission administer = owner
    permission members = owner + member
}

definition team {
    relation maintainer: user
    relation member: user | team#members
    permission members = maintainer + member
}

definition repository {
    relation org: organization
    relation admins: user | team#members
    relation maintainers: user | team#members
    relation writers: user | team#members
    relation readers: user | user:* | team#members | organization#members
    relation blocked: user
    permission admin = admins + org->administer
    permission maintain = admin + maintainers
    permission write = (maintain + writers) - blocked
    permission read = (write + readers) - blocked
}

# A Google-Docs-like model: an organisation, nested groups, a folder tree, documents with
# owners, editors, commenters, viewers, public links and blocks (an exclusion).

# Hand computation (members = {bob, carol, dave, erin, mallory}, eng = {bob, carol, dave}):
#   folder edit:  root {alice}; engineering eng ∪ {alice}; specs = engineering;
#                 design {erin, alice}; shared_ext {grace}
#   folder view:  root, engineering, specs, design = {alice} ∪ members;
#                 shared_ext {grace, frank, mallory}
#   roadmap   edit {alice};             view {alice} ∪ members
#   arch      edit {alice, bob, dave};  comment edit ∪ {frank};
#             view {alice, bob, dave, erin, mallory, frank}           (carol blocked)
#   mockups   edit {erin, alice};       comment edit ∪ eng;  view {alice} ∪ members
#   secret    edit {alice} ∪ eng;       view {alice, bob, carol, dave, erin}
#             (frank and mallory blocked through contractors)

assertions:
# `member & viewer`: both sides must hold; a wildcard on one side still needs the other.

# view(d) = {anne, bob} ∩ {anne, carol} = {anne}; view(p) = {dave} ∩ all = {dave}.

  assertTrue:
    - document:d#view@user:anne
    - document:p#view@user:dave
  assertFalse:
    - document:d#view@user:bob
    - document:d#view@user:carol
    - document:d#view@user:eve
    - document:p#view@user:anne
    - document:p#view@user:eve

document:d#member@user:bob

assertions:
# Tenant isolation: identical structures in two tenants; nothing leaks across except an
# explicit share.

# view(p1) = {a_lead, a_admin, a_user}; view(p2) = {b_admin, b_user}
# view(d1) = view(p1); view(d2) = view(p2); view(d3) = view(p1) ∪ {b_user}
assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - document:d1#view@user:a_user
    - document:d1#view@user:a_admin
    - document:d1#view@user:a_lead
    - project:p1#manage@user:a_admin
    - document:d2#view@user:b_user
    - document:d2#view@user:b_admin
    - document:d3#view@user:b_user
    - document:d3#view@user:a_user
  assertFalse:
    - document:d1#view@user:b_user
    - document:d1#view@user:b_admin
    - document:d2#view@user:a_admin
    - document:d2#view@user:a_user
    - document:d2#view@user:a_lead
    - document:d3#view@user:b_admin
    - project:p2#manage@user:a_admin
    - project:p1#manage@user:b_admin
    - project:p1#manage@user:a_user
relationships:
tenant:t1#admin@user:a_admin
tenant:t1#member@user:a_user
tenant:t2#admin@user:b_admin
tenant:t2#member@user:b_user
project:p1#tenant@tenant:t1
project:p1#lead@user:a_lead
project:p2#tenant@tenant:t2
document:d1#project@project:p1
document:d2#project@project:p2
document:d3#project@project:p1
// The one explicit cross-tenant share.
document:d3#viewer@user:b_user

assertions:
# Groups that contain each other (a ⊃ b ⊃ c ⊃ a) and a group that contains itself:
# check terminates with the least fixed point.

# a, b, c are one cycle, so S(a) = S(b) = S(c) = {bob, a#member, b#member, c#member}.
# S(x, member) = {x#member}: the self loop adds nothing.
assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - group:a#member@user:bob
    - group:b#member@user:bob
    - group:c#member@user:bob
    - group:a#member@group:c#member
    - group:c#member@group:b#member
    - document:d#view@user:bob
    - group:x#member@group:x#member
  assertFalse:
    - group:a#member@user:eve
    - group:c#member@user:eve
    - document:d#view@user:eve
    - group:x#member@user:bob
    - group:x#member@group:a#member
    - group:a#member@group:x#member

# Lookups walk the cycle backwards and stop: every group of the cycle once.
expectedLookups:
  resources:
    - query: "group#member@user:bob"
      expect: [a, b, c]
    - query: "group#member@group:a#member"
      expect: [a, b, c]
    - query: "group#member@group:x#member"
      expect: [x]
    - query: "group#member@user:eve"
      expect: []
    - query: "document#view@user:bob"
      expect: [d]
    - query: "document#view@group:c#member"
      expect: [d]
    - query: "document#view@user:eve"
      expect: []
  subjects:
    - query: "group:a#member@user"
      expect: { ids: [bob] }
    - query: "group:c#member@user"
      expect: { ids: [bob] }
    - query: "group:x#member@user"
      expect: { ids: [] }
    - query: "document:d#view@user"
      expect: { ids: [bob] }
relationships:
group:a#member@group:b#member
group:b#member@group:c#member
group:c#member@group:a#member
group:b#member@user:bob
group:x#member@group:x#member
document:d#viewer@group:a#member

assertions:
# A cycle through the subtracted side of an exclusion has no well-defined answer
# (docs/04-evaluation.md §3.6): the engine fails with NON_MONOTONIC_CYCLE when it reaches
# one, and answers normally on data where the cycle is not reached. The reference evaluator
# refuses this schema (it is not stratifiable), so assertions here are checked against the
# engine and the hand-computed answers only.

# view(y) = {u} \ ∅ = {u}; view(x) = {u} \ view(y) = ∅.
# For a user who is not a viewer, the base side is false and the cycle is never reached.
assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - doc:y#view@user:u
  assertFalse:
    - doc:x#view@user:u
    - doc:a#view@user:other
    - doc:b#view@user:other

expectCheckErrors:
  doc:a#view@user:u: NON_MONOTONIC_CYCLE
  doc:b#view@user:u: NON_MONOTONIC_CYCLE
  doc:c#view@user:u: NON_MONOTONIC_CYCLE
relationships:
// A self loop and a two-node cycle, both reached.
doc:a#parent@doc:a
doc:a#viewer@user:u
doc:b#parent@doc:c
doc:c#parent@doc:b
doc:b#viewer@user:u
doc:c#viewer@user:u
// Acyclic: x → y.
doc:x#parent@doc:y
doc:x#viewer@user:u
doc:y#viewer@user:u

assertions:
# Prefixed type names (`docs/document`, `iam/user`) are distinct from unprefixed ones.

# view(root) = {iam/user:anne}; view(readme) = {iam/user:bob, iam/user:anne};
# view(other) = {user:anne}.
assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - docs/document:readme#view@iam/user:anne
    - docs/document:readme#view@iam/user:bob
    - docs/folder:root#view@iam/user:anne
    - docs/document:other#view@user:anne
    - iam/group:eng#member@iam/user:anne
  assertFalse:
    - docs/document:readme#view@user:anne
    - docs/document:other#view@iam/user:anne
    - docs/folder:root#view@iam/user:bob
    - docs/document:readme#view@user:bob

# Self membership (docs/04-evaluation.md §2): `o#m` is always in S(o, m), with or without
# tuples, but `o#m` is not in S(o, m') for another member m' unless m' contains m.

# S(eng, member) = {anne, eng#member}; S(eng, is_member) = S(eng, member) ∪ {eng#is_member}.
assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - group:eng#member@group:eng#member
    - group:empty#member@group:empty#member
    - group:eng#is_member@group:eng#is_member
    - group:eng#is_member@group:eng#member
    - document:d#view@group:eng#member
    - document:d#view@user:anne
  assertFalse:
    - group:eng#member@group:other#member
    - group:eng#member@group:eng#is_member
    - group:empty#member@group:eng#member
    - document:d#view@group:other#member

# Subject sets: a document shared with `group:a#member`, where a ⊃ b ⊃ c (3 deep).

# S(c, member) = {carol, c#member}
# S(b, member) = {bob} ∪ S(c, member) ∪ {b#member}
# S(a, member) = {alice} ∪ S(b, member) ∪ {a#member}
# S(doc, view) = S(a, member) ∪ {doc#view, doc#viewer}; S(other, view) = S(c, member) ∪ ...
assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - document:doc#view@user:alice
    - document:doc#view@user:bob
    - document:doc#view@user:carol
    - group:a#member@user:carol
    - document:doc#view@group:c#member
    - document:doc#view@group:a#member
    - document:other#view@user:carol
  assertFalse:
    - document:other#view@user:bob
    - document:other#view@user:alice
    - document:other#view@group:a#member
    - group:c#member@user:alice
    - group:b#member@user:alice
    - group:c#member@group:b#member
    - document:doc#view@user:dave
relationships:
group:a#member@group:b#member
group:b#member@group:c#member
group:a#member@user:alice
group:b#member@user:bob
group:c#member@user:carol
document:doc#viewer@group:a#member
document:other#viewer@group:c#member

assertions:
# `user:*` matches every user, including ones no tuple mentions, but never a subject set
# and never another type.

# S(public, view)  = every user
# S(private, view) = {anne}
# S(team, view)    = {bob, group:eng#member}
assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - document:public#view@user:anne
    - document:public#viewer@user:bob
    - document:public#view@user:zed
    - document:private#view@user:anne
    - document:team#view@user:bob
    - document:team#view@group:eng#member
  assertFalse:
    - document:private#view@user:zed
    - document:public#view@group:eng#member
    - document:public#view@bot:r2
    - document:team#view@user:anne
    - document:team#view@user:zed

# Lookups: the wildcard answers "every user" (subject type user only).
expectedLookups:
  subjects:
    - query: "document:public#view@user"
      expect: { wildcard: true, excluded: [] }
    - query: "document:public#view@bot"
      expect: { ids: [] }
    - query: "document:private#view@user"
      expect: { ids: [anne] }
    - query: "document:team#view@user"
      expect: { ids: [bob] }

# A stored wildcard `t:*` matches objects of type `t`, never a subject set `t:x#r`
# (docs/04-evaluation.md §3.3). SpiceDB matches the subject set too: KD-3 in
# crates/pemba-difftest/KNOWN_DIFFERENCES.md. On the grant side pemba says false where
# SpiceDB says true. On the subtracted side of an exclusion pemba would say true where
# SpiceDB says false, so it fails with AMBIGUOUS_WILDCARD_EXCLUSION instead (T3.4b,
# docs/04-evaluation.md §3.3).

assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - doc:d#viewer@grp:g
    - doc:d#viewer@grp:anyone
  assertFalse:
    # Grant side: the wildcard does not match the subject set.
    - doc:d#viewer@grp:g#member
    # Only the subject set grp:g#member is a viewer, not the object grp:g.
    - page:p#view@grp:g
    # No viewer: the exclusion's base is empty, so its subtracted side is never reached.
    - page:q#view@grp:g#member

expectCheckErrors:
  # Subtracted side: grp:* bans every grp object; whether it bans the subject set is
  # ambiguous (SpiceDB: yes).
  page:p#view@grp:g#member: AMBIGUOUS_WILDCARD_EXCLUSION
